answer: Inlet-Paired Execution Ledger: each identity must submit work through a unique low-traffic input channel whose history is cross-checked against a shared execution log. Duplicates surface when two identities claim the same channel lineage, since the log preserves every prior route like strata in a glacier. An attacker must therefore provision and sustain a distinct channel history per fake identity, reaching a cost nadir only at large scale. Each fabricated identity costs a separate maintained channel plus continuous log reconciliation, making duplication visible and expensive.
